clue.text: Bin the last of Geraldine's pickle

definitions.note: a pickle is a fix or predicament, as is a scrape

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away, to scrap it

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the following word only

parts.note: the name Geraldine, its 's read as is linking to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a jar of Geraldine's homemade pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an awkward situation or predicament one has got oneself into.

clue.text: Street fight cancelled

parts.note: a ruck is a rough scrum or brawl

explanation.surface: A street brawl is called off before it starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A deleted item is struck out or struck off, so the past participle means removed or annulled.

clue.text: Large dog, good during journey home

indicators.note: the letter for good sits within the phrase, as if happening during the trip

parts.note: a ride back is a trip home

explanation.surface: A big dog behaves well on the trip back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhodesian ridgeback is a large hunting breed with a ridge of reversed hair along its spine.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridgeback is a big hound breed originally from southern Africa, an example of a large dog.

clue.text: Timid lady famous for singing comes up to piano

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: A shy singer edges nervously up to the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: PAVID is a rare word from Latin pavidus, fearful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavid is a literary adjective meaning fearful or easily frightened, a synonym of timid.

clue.text: Jumping in is too cold, equally salty

indicators.note: the letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A swimmer hesitates at the edge: diving in is too cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotonic solution has the same salt concentration as another, such as body fluid, hence equal saltiness.

clue.text: Saucepan burned stews far too much

indicators.note: to stew is to cook and churn together, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook overdoes the stewing until the saucepan is scorched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burned' reads as part of the kitchen disaster but is fodder; the anagram signal is 'stews'.
explanation.definitionFit: Superabundance is an excess, a quantity far greater than needed.

clue.text: Audibly have a bash on old German's percussion

indicators.note: the first word is taken by its sound, spelt differently

parts.note: to have a bash at something is to try it
the Angles were a Germanic people who settled in England; read as old Germans

explanation.surface: Someone loudly takes a swing at an elderly German man's drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old German's' is read as plural, the Angles, the ancient Germanic tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are struck metal instruments in an orchestra's percussion section.

clue.text: Canteen provided society for drinkers, any number turning up

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: if means provided that
AA is Alcoholics Anonymous
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A works canteen laid on a drinking club, and any number showed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI is the organisation running canteens and shops for the British armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The NAAFI operates refreshment facilities for British service personnel, so the word stands for a military canteen.

clue.text: Indians nomadic hence carrying foreign money

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the currency inside them
wandering, so the letters roam into a new order

parts.note: the word hence, taken as written
the yen is the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Wandering tribespeople are carrying some foreign cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains, called Indians in older usage.

clue.text: Two options to stop striker lifting equipment?

definitions.meaning: a defender can block a shot or tackle the forward
a system of pulleys and rope used to hoist loads

explanation.walkthrough: In football a striker is the attacking forward; the two defensive moves together name the hoisting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A block and tackle is a pulley assembly that gives mechanical advantage for raising heavy weights.

clue.text: Ruby perhaps cut sandwiches the day before — make fresh?

indicators.note: the two outer words hold the inner one between them like bread

parts.note: ruby is a shade of red
to lop is to cut off
eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: Ruby slices up yesterday's sandwiches to make them look fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruby' looks like a woman's name but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To redevelop is to build or work something anew, renovating it.

clue.text: Sorcerer on island is character for show

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: a mage is a wizard

explanation.surface: A wizard living on an island is a showman of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is the public persona someone presents, a character put on for display.

clue.text: Pretty short of time, so prompt

indicators.note: lacking, so the letter for time drops out

parts.note: cute means attractive

explanation.surface: An actor quite lacking in time is given a prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like the adverb, as in pretty short, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal to an actor to speak or enter, a prompt.

clue.text: Impractical, dreadful clutches affected Cortina

indicators.note: the outer word grips the inner letters

parts.note: dire means terrible

indicators.note: acted upon and altered, so the letters change order

parts.note: the car name Cortina, taken as written

explanation.surface: A clapped-out Ford Cortina has a dreadful clutch, making it impractical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cortina was a popular Ford family car in Britain from the 1960s to 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire person applies theory rigidly without regard for practicality.

clue.text: When tailed, quick agents dash

indicators.note: the word has its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: fast means quick
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Followed by a tail, the spies make a quick getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' is short for dashboard; 'tailed' sounds like being followed but means losing an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is the instrument panel of a car, also called the dashboard.

clue.text: Head of marketing docked £1,000 by company's calculation

parts.note: CO is company; the 's is read as is

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the word marketing, whose head is M
a ship that puts in has docked at a port
a grand is a thousand pounds, abbreviated G

explanation.surface: The marketing chief has his pay cut by a thousand pounds, by the firm's reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks like a pay cut but means a ship arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing is the act of working out figures, a calculation.

clue.text: PM unlocked success?

parts.note: without locks of hair, hence hairless
a win

explanation.surface: A prime minister breaks open a lock and succeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was British prime minister three times between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Baldwin led the UK government in the 1920s and 1930s, a Conservative prime minister.

clue.text: Vessel with lid full of bitter, nasty smell

indicators.note: the hat contains the other pieces

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
bitter is a British style of ale
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A pint pot with a lid is brimming with bitter beer and smells foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a tankard in this scene; it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaleboat is a long, narrow rowing boat once used in whaling, a type of craft.

clue.text: Rats disembarked for launch

parts.note: rats and blast are both mild exclamations of annoyance
people who have disembarked are off the ship

explanation.surface: Rodents scurry off the ship ahead of its launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Blast-off is the moment a rocket lifts away, its launch into flight.

clue.text: Love beastly mother returned furiously

parts.note: to like is a milder form of loving

indicators.note: sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: An animal mother comes back in a rage over her love.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like mad means doing it with frantic energy, a colloquial idiom for furiously.

clue.text: New supermarket opening in Queens offers American exchange

parts.note: Asda is a British supermarket chain

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word Queens, whose opening letter is Q

explanation.surface: A new store launches in the New York borough of Queens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nasdaq is a US stock market, an electronic exchange based in New York.

clue.text: Enthusiastic singer, quivering treble

indicators.note: shaking, so the letters are shaken into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A keen chorister's high voice wobbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A belter is someone who sings loudly and forcefully, belting out a song.

clue.text: Japanese vessels saw Sumatra out east

indicators.note: the letters come out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Japanese ships sight Sumatra out to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships at sea; here they are pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Satsuma ware is a style of Japanese pottery with crackled glaze, so the vessels are ceramics.

clue.text: Oven needs higher temperature for grill

indicators.note: in a down answer, higher means placed above the other piece

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: The oven needs turning up to grill the food.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast is to brown under direct heat, the same as to grill bread.

clue.text: Times table finally clear

parts.note: eras are periods of time

indicators.note: take only the end letter of the word

parts.note: the word table, whose final letter is E

explanation.surface: The times table is finally wiped off the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times table' reads as one phrase but splits at the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or remove, as in clearing a board.

clue.text: Pay close attention to the first person you hear

indicators.note: the word is as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Listen closely to whoever speaks first.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch it carefully, keeping close attention on it.

clue.text: Arab shortly coming over

indicators.note: turning over, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: in a mo means in a moment, soon

explanation.surface: An Arab visitor will be arriving soon.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman on the Arabian Peninsula, an Arab national.

clue.text: Thrill with fight after a football game

indicators.note: the fight comes after the letter A

parts.note: a kick is a buzz of excitement
taken as written
a bout is a boxing match

explanation.surface: A match that is all excitement and scuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickabout is an informal game of football, a casual kick of a ball.

clue.text: Large and one supposes, slightly shorter overalls

parts.note: fat means large

indicators.note: trimmed by one letter at the end

parts.note: guess means suppose

explanation.surface: A big guy reckons his overalls have shrunk a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigues are loose military work clothing, worn like overalls.

clue.text: Harry back in Montecito after court, in that woman's embrace

indicators.note: together with embrace, the woman's arms enclose the other pieces
an embrace surrounds, so the pronoun wraps around the rest

parts.note: her is the female pronoun

indicators.note: the final letter follows the court letters
the back of the word is its last letter

parts.note: the place name Montecito, whose last letter is O

explanation.surface: Prince Harry, back home in Montecito after a court case, is held by his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Harry lives in Montecito, California; 'Harry' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or badger, as to harry is to harass persistently.
